questions.q: Do I need an accountant?
questions.a: An accountant helps you stay compliant, avoid penalties, meet every deadline and make better financial decisions, so you can spend your time running your business.

questions.q: Which services do you offer?
questions.a: We provide quarterly VAT returns, monthly payroll, annual accounts and Corporation Tax returns, and Self Assessment tax returns for UK businesses and individuals.

questions.q: How much do your services cost?
questions.a: Every business is different, so we don't publish fixed prices. After a free consultation we send you a clear quote based on exactly what you need, agreed before any work starts.

questions.q: What affects the price?
questions.a: Mainly the size and complexity of your business: the number of transactions, how many people you pay, your VAT scheme, the state of your records and how many services you need.

questions.q: How do I switch to ZFK Accountants?
questions.a: We contact your previous accountant, collect the records we need and manage the handover, so your deadlines and filings carry on without a gap.

questions.q: Do I need to visit an office?
questions.a: No. We work entirely online. Consultations happen by video call, documents are shared securely online and you approve everything digitally.

questions.q: Do you work with clients across the UK?
questions.a: Yes. Because everything is online, we work with businesses and individuals anywhere in the UK.

questions.q: How do I book a consultation?
questions.a: Use the booking form on our contact page to choose a date and time that suits you. We'll email you within one working day to confirm and send the call details.

questions.q: Is the consultation really free?
questions.a: Yes. The first consultation is free and there is no obligation. It's a chance to talk through your needs before we send a quote.

questions.q: How do I share my documents?
questions.a: We share a secure online space for your records, or connect to your cloud accounting software, so nothing needs to be posted or emailed unprotected.

categories.name: Data & Security
categories.desc: How we keep your records safe

questions.q: How is my information protected?
questions.a: Your records are kept in secure, access-controlled cloud storage and used only to provide the services you've asked us for. We never sell or share them for marketing.

questions.q: Do I need to register for VAT?
questions.a: You must register if your VAT-taxable turnover goes over £90,000 in any rolling twelve months, or you expect it to in the next thirty days. You can also register voluntarily.

questions.q: What is Making Tax Digital?
questions.a: Making Tax Digital requires VAT-registered businesses to keep digital records and submit VAT returns through compatible software.

questions.q: How often are VAT returns due?
questions.a: Most businesses file a VAT return every quarter. Each return and payment is usually due one month and seven days after the end of the VAT period.

questions.q: Can you submit my VAT returns?
questions.a: Yes. We prepare, review and submit your quarterly VAT returns through Making Tax Digital, and you approve each one before it is filed.

questions.q: Can you run my monthly payroll?
questions.a: Yes. We run payroll every month, produce payslips, send Real Time Information to HMRC and tell you what PAYE to pay and when.

questions.q: Can you run payroll for just me as a director?
questions.a: Yes. Many limited company directors take a salary through PAYE. We run it monthly and keep it in line with your wider tax position.

questions.q: Do you handle workplace pensions?
questions.a: Yes. We assess staff for auto-enrolment and calculate pension contributions every pay run.

questions.q: Can you take over from my current payroll provider?
questions.a: Yes. We collect your year-to-date figures and employee details so the switch happens with no break in pay.

questions.q: What are annual accounts?
questions.a: Annual accounts are statutory financial statements filed with Companies House and used to calculate your company's Corporation Tax.

questions.q: When do I need to file my accounts?
questions.a: Most private limited companies must file annual accounts within nine months of the end of their financial year.

questions.q: When is Corporation Tax due?
questions.a: For most small and medium companies, Corporation Tax is due nine months and one day after the end of the accounting period, and the CT600 return twelve months after it.

questions.q: Can you prepare my Corporation Tax return?
questions.a: Yes. We prepare your accounts and CT600 together, calculate the tax due and file both on time.

questions.q: Who needs to complete a Self Assessment?
questions.a: Usually sole traders, partners, landlords, company directors with untaxed income such as dividends, and anyone with other untaxed income or gains.

questions.q: When is the Self Assessment deadline?
questions.a: Online returns are due by 31 January after the end of the tax year, which is also when any tax owed must be paid.

questions.q: Can you help reduce mistakes on my tax return?
questions.a: Yes. We check your figures carefully, claim the allowances and expenses you're entitled to and file your return correctly and on time.

questions.q: What records should I keep?
questions.a: Keep records of your income, expense receipts, bank statements and any documents relating to your tax position, usually for at least five years after the filing deadline.
